data.narrative:
C12 Quantum Electronics is a Series A quantum computing company that has raised $19.4M to date. The valuation universe comprises 11 peers across quantum computing—3 public companies (IonQ, Rigetti Computing, D-Wave Quantum) and 8 private firms including Quantinuum and Infleqtion—though same-stage comparable data remains sparse in this sector.

A stage-progression methodology was the sole applicable triangulation approach. Using total capital raised ($19.4M) as a baseline proxy for Series A valuation, a standard 2.0x step-up multiplier to Series B was applied, implying a post-money valuation of $39M. Peer-median analysis could not be deployed: while 6 same-sector comps exist, filtering for stage, timing, and valuation-tier alignment yielded insufficient datapoints (threshold: ≥3) to construct a reliable comparable set. Relying on all-sector medians would introduce unacceptable noise given quantum computing's heterogeneous business models and maturity profiles.

The analysis supports a valuation range of $33M to $45M, with a median point estimate of $39M. This range reflects ±15% variance around the stage-progression result. Key uncertainties include the absence of direct same-stage peers for cross-validation, the nascent state of quantum computing commercialization, and whether total raised serves as an adequate Series A valuation proxy. The single-method result should be stress-tested against management guidance, burn dynamics, and any emerging late-stage or IPO comparables as the sector matures.
